first.title: Welcome
first.welcome.title: Turn your files into knowledge an agent can use
first.welcome.body: Drop in documents. Super Ontology finds the people, projects and decisions in them, keeps every fact tied to its source, and lets any agent read it with a single token. Everything stays on this computer.

first.reading.waiting: Waiting for the files to arrive…
first.reading.leave: You can leave. It keeps going.

first.agent.title: Give an agent access
first.agent.body: Create a read-only token, then copy the configuration into the agent you use.

import.review.title: The Builder is waiting for your review
import.review.body: It read your tables and proposed entities and relationships. Nothing is published until you confirm.
import.done.title: Imported and published
import.done.body: The ontology is live. Open it in the Atlas, read its files, or query the tables.
import.done.gateway: The Query tab is not connected to a Gateway yet. Connect one there with the token file that oo created.
import.hint.san: The database certificate must list the name the runtime uses to reach it (for a local database: host.docker.internal) as a subject alternative name, and carry the serverAuth usage. Reissue the certificate, then add the source again.
import.hint.grant: The database account is missing a permission. Ask your database administrator to run the statements shown by Run doctor, then try again.
import.hint.model: The model did not answer, or refused its key. Check the model in Settings, Model, then try again; the import continues where it stopped.
buildReview.title: Review what was found
buildReview.description: {name}: check what the Builder proposed. Nothing is published until you confirm.
buildReview.summaryNote: {declared, plural, one {# foreign key} other {# foreign keys}} declared by the database; {discovered, plural, =0 {no other candidates} one {# candidate} other {# candidates}} found by comparing values.
buildReview.sensitive: {hidden} of {checked} columns are hidden as sensitive.
buildReview.partial.title: Relationship search was cut short
buildReview.partial.body: {count, plural, one {# candidate was} other {# candidates were}} not checked. You can publish now and rebuild later.
buildReview.entitiesHelp: One entity per table, identified by its key.
buildReview.relationsHelp: A relationship lets a question join two tables. Accept the ones that are true; reject the ones that are coincidence.
buildReview.noRelations: No relationships were proposed. Each table is published on its own.
buildReview.origin.declared.help: Foreign keys the database enforces. The data agrees with them.
buildReview.origin.named.help: Columns whose names and values line up.
buildReview.origin.discovered.help: No key and no name link these columns. Accept one only if you know it is true.
buildReview.why.declared: The database declares this foreign key, and every row agrees with it.
buildReview.why.noSignal: The values fit, but nothing else links {from} to {to}: no declared key, no matching name. Small numeric ids often overlap by chance.
buildReview.why.strict: Every value of {from} is found in {to}, and {to} is unique.
buildReview.why.signal: Most values of {from} are found in {to}, and the column names agree.
buildReview.evidence.name: name match {percent}%
buildReview.fanout: Accepting this would multiply rows in a JOIN, so it cannot be accepted.
buildReview.confirmHelp: Your decision is written as a review file and the build continues: publish, start the Gateway, create your access.
buildReview.reason.default: Reviewed in the app: relationships checked against the data.
buildReview.changes: {count, plural, one {# decision differs from the proposal.} other {# decisions differ from the proposal.}}
